title: Introduce dependency-validate quick-verify mode and lightweight CI test stub runner
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Our CI has been spending increasing time on full dependency audits and heavy integration test runs for every dependency bump and small tooling change. This PR introduces a new lightweight 'quick-verify' mode for the dependency validator and a minimal CI test stub runner that gives fast feedback for infra/CI-only changes. The goals are: reduce turnaround for repo hygiene PRs, lower CI compute cost for dependency churn, and provide a safer incremental path for rolling out stricter dependency gates.

Implementation: 1) dep-validate: add a --quick-verify flag which performs checksum/manifest checks and a targeted transitive-safety probe instead of the full graph resolution. This is implemented in scripts/dep-validate with feature-flag gating (ENV: DEP_VALIDATE_QUICK=true) and returns structured exit codes documented in docs/ci/dependency-validation.md. 2) ci-stubber: add a new job template .github/workflows/ci-stub.yml and a small Go binary tools/ci-stubber that runs a configurable subset of smoke checks (lint-shard header, small unit test subset, and install/build dry-run) in memory without launching containers. The stub runner is intentionally conservative: it cannot replace full integration tests but detects common infra regressions early. 3) CI orchestration: add a conditional premerge lane that picks the stub runner for PRs touching only non-runtime paths (scripts/, .github/, build/) using a path-aware matcher. 4) Telemetry and rollback: emit metrics to observability when quick-verify is used and add a transparent opt-out via PR label 'ci:full' that forces the full CI path.

Files changed: workflow templates, a ~700 line script refactor for dep validator with unit tests, the small Go stub binary (approx 150 LOC), and docs updates describing usage and failure modes.

Testing: Local unit tests for dep-validate quick mode and e2e smoke in a constrained ephemeral runner were added. CI matrix includes the new ci-stub job and a staged rollout where the quick-verify job runs alongside full CI for the first 48 hours for telemetry validation. Manual canary on the redwood repo integration team was performed.

Rollout and risks: Quick-verify is opt-in via env and annotated in PR checks. Risk: false negatives where quick-verify misses a deep transitive issue. Mitigation: keep quick-verify as a fast pre-merge gate only; full CI remains the final blocker. Observability alerts added to detect divergence between quick-verify and full CI.

Related work: builds on design notes from ENG-1409 and complements the staged CI lanes introduced in ENG-2871. Linear: ENG-5212.

Checklist: - [x] Add --quick-verify implementation and docs. - [x] Add ci-stub job + binary. - [x] Add path matcher rules. - [x] Add telemetry hooks and opt-out label. - [x] Unit and smoke tests + staged rollout plan.
commits: 3 commits: 1) feat(dep-validate): add quick-verify mode and unit tests (Maya Chen) 2) chore(ci): add ci-stub template and path-aware matcher (Maya Chen) 3) feat(tools): introduce ci-stubber binary and integration fixture (Maya Chen)
ci_status: pass (one rerun of flaky lint shard required)
review_comments: Arjun: Please add explicit fallback behavior when DEP_VALIDATE_QUICK is unset. Response: implemented default to full validation unless env is set to true.
Sofia: Could quick-verify produce a false sense of safety? Suggest telemetry. Response: added metric emission and 48h dual-run rollout plan.
Liam: Can the stub runner accidentally mask container-level failures? Response: documented limitations in docs/ci/ci-stub-runner.md and added opt-out label 'ci:full'.
release_notes: Introduce a lightweight dependency quick-verify mode and a CI stub runner to speed feedback for infra changes. This is opt-in and intended as a pre-merge gate; full CI remains required. See docs/ci/* for usage.
